chunks: I wonder at the miser who is speeding towards the very destitution from which he wants to run away and misses the very ease of life which he covets. Consequently, he passes his life in this world like the destitute, but will have to render an account in the next world like the rich.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and practical paradox of miserliness according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the existential paradox of the miser who, by hoarding wealth, denies himself its utility and thus lives in a state of functional poverty, yet remains liable for its spiritual accounting as the wealthy are. This reflection underscores the Shia emphasis on *barakah* (divine blessing) over mere accumulation, illustrating how stinginess corrupts the soul's readiness for the Hereafter. The commentary links this folly to the broader theme of *zuhd* (asceticism) not as destitution, but as the proper utilization of resources for divine purposes.
